newsitem.title: USA: Greenpeace activists arrested for blocking grain terminal.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace activists arrested for blocking grain terminal.

text.p: Seventeen people from the environmental group Greenpeace were arrested Thursday for disrupting grain loadings at a terminal here in a protest over genetically altered soybeans, authorities said.
Nine protestors chained themselves to the front gate of the Archer Daniels Midland Co. terminal while eight others chained themselves inside two soybean barges, police and Greenpeace officials said.

By midday, authorities were still working to cut loose four of the protestors inside the barges, Greenpeace spokesman Paul Clarke told Reuters. The other 13 had been cut free and booked. He said all 17 were charged with criminal trespass.
Greenpeace said in a statement that its activists had "occupied" the Destrehan facility and halted loadings to protest exports of genetically altered soybeans.
"Today's action marks Day Four of the week-long Greenpeace protest against the release of genetically engineered soybeans into the marketplace," the statement said.

The altered soybeans are designed to tolerate Monsanto Co.'s "Roundup Ready" herbicide. Greenpeace maintains the altered soybeans were not adequately tested before being approved for human consumption.
"At the very least they should be separated and labeled as genetically engineered so consumers can choose whether they want to buy them," Greenpeace spokeswoman Terri Johnson said.
An ADM employee at the terminal who declined to be named said, "They (protestors) are all over the place out here." Greenpeace said 25 protestors went to the grain terminal.
"We are not loading right now. We have the police department out here," the ADM employee said before hanging up.
An ADM spokesman at the company's headquarters in Decatur, Ill., was not available to comment.
The Destrehan terminal has storage capacity of more than 6 million bushels and a loading rate of 50,000 bushels an hour, according to industry sources.

Greenpeace said its activists, wearing white hard hats and blue overalls with "Genetic Experiment" written on them, climbed into and attached themselves to 200-foot-long soybean barges at the terminal at about 9:30 a.m. CST (1530 GMT).
The ADM employee said the facility was loading corn when the protestors arrived.
